followup_explanation:
This is a constrained extraction/synthesis task: pull evidence from given sources, answer two specific questions, produce one tight paragraph with a clear completion criterion ("don't ramble"). My choice was driven mostly by capability, since neither model's task preferences strongly favor this kind of work.

On the benchmarks, Willet-235B leads across the board — MMLU-Pro (81.2 vs 75.9), Arena-Hard (90.6 vs 83.2), IFEval (89.8 vs 85.3, relevant to following the format constraints), and notably the internal Extraction & Retrieval and Summarization evals (85.3/86.4 vs 79.2/80.6). Since this task is essentially evidence-grounded summarization with strict format requirements, Willet's stronger profile in exactly those categories made it the better fit.

The task-preference notes weren't decisive here. Lapwing self-reports preferring well-specified, low-latitude tasks like this one, but the documentation explicitly says those preferences are dissociated from output quality. So I weighted measured capability over self-reported preference, which pointed to Willet.
